== widgets.toml
# Herd widgets: one worker per ready issue under .scratch/ in this repo.
# Written by `loopherd init`; yours to edit. loopherd changes it only on a yes to `loopherd herd upgrade`.
repo = "<root>/widgets"
args = ["--permission-mode", "auto"]

[queue]
template = "issue"
# Prints "<id> <type> <skill> <slug> <path>" per issue file on origin/main under
# .scratch/<feature>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md whose Status: line has
# ready-for-agent and none of blocked, needs-info, ready-for-human,
# resolved, closed or done, and whose Blocked by: line names only resolved
# issues of its feature, or of the feature the issue path before each number
# names. The id is <feature>-<NN>; a feature that isn't
# lowercase letters, digits and - or doesn't fit the member name is cut and
# takes a 3-character hash, as <cut>_<hash>-<NN>, rehashed when another
# feature holds it. The Status: words act as labels: types maps one to the branch
# type (else feat), and skill:<name> names the worker's skill (else tdd).
source = '''
git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || git fetch -q origin main || exit
files=$(git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- .scratch) || exit
issue='^\.scratch/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/issues/[0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.md$'
printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -E '^"?\.scratch/.+/issues/[^/]+\.md"?$' | grep -vE "$issue" \
  | sed 's|.*|skipped &: an issue path is .scratch/<feature>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md of letters, digits and . _ -|' >&2
printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -E "$issue" | while read -r f; do
  printf '\n\036%s\n' "$f"
  git show "origin/main:$f"
done | awk -v room=24 -v list=ready '
  BEGIN {
    types["bug"] = "fix"; types["documentation"] = "docs"
    b36 = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    chars = b36 "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ._-"
  }
  { sub(/\r$/, "") }
  function has(f, label) { return index(labels[f], " " label " ") > 0 }
  function closed(f) { return has(f, "resolved") || has(f, "closed") || has(f, "done") }
  function value(line) { sub(/^[^:]*:/, "", line); gsub(/[*`]/, " ", line); return line }
  function unblocked(f,    items, k, i, item, said, words, w, j, n, of, b, found, dir) {
    if (!(f in blockers) || blockers[f] ~ /^[ \t,]*(none|$)/) return 1
    k = split(blockers[f], items, /[,;]/)
    for (i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
      item = items[i]
      if (item ~ /^[ \t]*$/) continue
      said = item
      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", said)
      # An item names the numbers in its first run of number-words, joined
      # by and, & or /: not a title in parentheses, after a colon or after
      # the run, nor a slug past the leading number.
      gsub(/\([^)]*\)/, " ", item)
      sub(/:.*/, "", item)
      of = feature[f]
      # Each path becomes one \001<dir> word naming the feature of the numbers
      # after it. Only a bare ./issues/ or ../issues/ names the feature of the
      # issue itself; a longer path ending in . or .. names none.
      while (match(item, /[^ \t]*\/issues\//)) {
        dir = substr(item, RSTART, RLENGTH - 8)
        if (dir !~ /^\.\.?$/ && sub(/.*\//, "", dir) && dir ~ /^\.\.?$/) dir = ""
        item = substr(item, 1, RSTART - 1) " \001" dir " " substr(item, RSTART + RLENGTH)
      }
      gsub(/(^|[ \t])issues\//, " ", item)
      w = split(item, words, /[ \t\/]+/)
      found = 0
      for (j = 1; j <= w; j++) {
        if (words[j] ~ /^\001/) {
          dir = substr(words[j], 2)
          of = dir ~ /^\.\.?$/ ? feature[f] : features[dir]
          continue
        }
        if (words[j] !~ /^#?[0-9]/) {
          if (found && words[j] !~ /^(and|&|\+)?$/) break
          continue
        }
        n = words[j]
        sub(/^#/, "", n)
        sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", n)
        b = issue[of "/" (n + 0)]
        if (b == "") {
          if (of == feature[f]) print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by names " n ", which is no issue of its feature" > "/dev/stderr"
          else print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by names " said ", which is no issue" > "/dev/stderr"
          return 0
        }
        if (!closed(b)) return 0
        found = 1
      }
      if (!found) {
        print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by item \"" said "\" names no issue number" > "/dev/stderr"
        return 0
      }
    }
    return 1
  }
  function hash(s,    i, n) {
    n = 0
    for (i = 1; i <= length(s); i++) n = (n * 67 + index(chars, substr(s, i, 1))) % 46656
    return substr(b36, int(n / 1296) + 1, 1) substr(b36, int(n / 36) % 36 + 1, 1) substr(b36, n % 36 + 1, 1)
  }
  function id_of(f,    id, cut, salt) {
    id = tolower(feature[f])
    gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-", id)
    gsub(/^-+|-+$/, "", id)
    if (id == feature[f] && length(id) + 1 + length(num[f]) <= room) return id
    cut = substr(id, 1, room - length(num[f]) - 5)
    gsub(/-+$/, "", cut)
    # Another feature on the same hashed id rehashes, so no two share one.
    salt = ""
    id = cut "_" hash(feature[f])
    while ((id in owner) && owner[id] != feature[f]) id = cut "_" hash(feature[f] "#" ++salt)
    owner[id] = feature[f]
    return id
  }
  /^\036/ {
    f = substr($0, 2)
    files[++n] = f
    split(f, part, "/")
    feature[f] = part[2]
    features[tolower(part[2])] = part[2]
    name[f] = part[4]
    num[f] = name[f]
    sub(/-.*/, "", num[f])
    issue[part[2] "/" (num[f] + 0)] = f
    comments = 0
    listing = 0
    next
  }
  { line = tolower($0) }
  line ~ /^#+[ \t]*comments[ \t]*$/ { comments = 1 }
  comments { next }
  !(f in title) && /^#[ \t]/ {
    title[f] = $0
    sub(/^#[ \t]+/, "", title[f]); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", title[f])
  }
  !(f in labels) && line ~ /^[ \t*_]*status[ \t*_]*:/ {
    s = value(line)
    gsub(/[ \t,]+/, " ", s)
    labels[f] = " " s " "
  }
  listing && line ~ /^[ \t]*[-*+][ \t]/ {
    sub(/^[ \t]*[-*+][ \t]+/, "", line)
    blockers[f] = blockers[f] "," line
    next
  }
  listing && line !~ /^[ \t]*$/ { listing = 0 }
  !(f in blockers) && line ~ /^[ \t*_]*blocked by[ \t*_]*:/ {
    blockers[f] = value(line)
    listing = blockers[f] ~ /^[ \t]*$/
  }
  END {
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) ids[files[i]] = id_of(files[i])
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
      f = files[i]
      if (list == "backlog") {
        if (has(f, "blocked") || closed(f)) continue
        if (has(f, "ready-for-agent") && !has(f, "needs-info") \
            && !has(f, "ready-for-human")) continue
        if (!unblocked(f)) continue
        if (!(f in title)) { title[f] = name[f]; sub(/\.md$/, "", title[f]) }
        print f, title[f]
        continue
      }
      if (!has(f, "ready-for-agent") || has(f, "blocked") || has(f, "needs-info") \
          || has(f, "ready-for-human") || closed(f) || !unblocked(f)) continue
      type = "feat"; skill = "tdd"
      k = split(labels[f], words, " ")
      for (j = k; j >= 1; j--) {
        if (words[j] in types) type = types[words[j]]
        if (words[j] ~ /^skill:[a-z0-9._:-]+$/) skill = substr(words[j], 7)
      }
      slug = tolower(name[f])
      sub(/^[0-9]+-/, "", slug); sub(/\.md$/, "", slug)
      gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, " ", slug)
      k = split(slug, words, " ")
      slug = ""
      for (j = 1; j <= k && j <= 5; j++) slug = slug (j > 1 ? "-" : "") words[j]
      if (slug == "") slug = "issue"
      id = ids[f]
      if (length(id) + 1 + length(num[f]) > room) {
        print "skipped " f ": the herd name leaves no room for its id" > "/dev/stderr"
        continue
      }
      id = id "-" num[f]
      print id, type, skill, slug, f
    }
  }'
'''
# Prints "<path> <title>" per open issue file the source leaves out, but for
# blocked ones: its Status: line has neither ready-for-agent, blocked,
# resolved, closed nor done, or has needs-info or ready-for-human, and its
# Blocked by: line names only resolved issues. The title is its first
# # heading, else the file's name. Ones waiting on the human stay: they are
# what a dry queue forgets.
backlog = '''
git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || git fetch -q origin main || exit
files=$(git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main -- .scratch) || exit
issue='^\.scratch/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/issues/[0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.md$'
printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -E '^"?\.scratch/.+/issues/[^/]+\.md"?$' | grep -vE "$issue" \
  | sed 's|.*|skipped &: an issue path is .scratch/<feature>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md of letters, digits and . _ -|' >&2
printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -E "$issue" | while read -r f; do
  printf '\n\036%s\n' "$f"
  git show "origin/main:$f"
done | awk -v room=24 -v list=backlog '
  BEGIN {
    types["bug"] = "fix"; types["documentation"] = "docs"
    b36 = "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    chars = b36 "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ._-"
  }
  { sub(/\r$/, "") }
  function has(f, label) { return index(labels[f], " " label " ") > 0 }
  function closed(f) { return has(f, "resolved") || has(f, "closed") || has(f, "done") }
  function value(line) { sub(/^[^:]*:/, "", line); gsub(/[*`]/, " ", line); return line }
  function unblocked(f,    items, k, i, item, said, words, w, j, n, of, b, found, dir) {
    if (!(f in blockers) || blockers[f] ~ /^[ \t,]*(none|$)/) return 1
    k = split(blockers[f], items, /[,;]/)
    for (i = 1; i <= k; i++) {
      item = items[i]
      if (item ~ /^[ \t]*$/) continue
      said = item
      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", said)
      # An item names the numbers in its first run of number-words, joined
      # by and, & or /: not a title in parentheses, after a colon or after
      # the run, nor a slug past the leading number.
      gsub(/\([^)]*\)/, " ", item)
      sub(/:.*/, "", item)
      of = feature[f]
      # Each path becomes one \001<dir> word naming the feature of the numbers
      # after it. Only a bare ./issues/ or ../issues/ names the feature of the
      # issue itself; a longer path ending in . or .. names none.
      while (match(item, /[^ \t]*\/issues\//)) {
        dir = substr(item, RSTART, RLENGTH - 8)
        if (dir !~ /^\.\.?$/ && sub(/.*\//, "", dir) && dir ~ /^\.\.?$/) dir = ""
        item = substr(item, 1, RSTART - 1) " \001" dir " " substr(item, RSTART + RLENGTH)
      }
      gsub(/(^|[ \t])issues\//, " ", item)
      w = split(item, words, /[ \t\/]+/)
      found = 0
      for (j = 1; j <= w; j++) {
        if (words[j] ~ /^\001/) {
          dir = substr(words[j], 2)
          of = dir ~ /^\.\.?$/ ? feature[f] : features[dir]
          continue
        }
        if (words[j] !~ /^#?[0-9]/) {
          if (found && words[j] !~ /^(and|&|\+)?$/) break
          continue
        }
        n = words[j]
        sub(/^#/, "", n)
        sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", n)
        b = issue[of "/" (n + 0)]
        if (b == "") {
          if (of == feature[f]) print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by names " n ", which is no issue of its feature" > "/dev/stderr"
          else print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by names " said ", which is no issue" > "/dev/stderr"
          return 0
        }
        if (!closed(b)) return 0
        found = 1
      }
      if (!found) {
        print "skipped " f ": its Blocked by item \"" said "\" names no issue number" > "/dev/stderr"
        return 0
      }
    }
    return 1
  }
  function hash(s,    i, n) {
    n = 0
    for (i = 1; i <= length(s); i++) n = (n * 67 + index(chars, substr(s, i, 1))) % 46656
    return substr(b36, int(n / 1296) + 1, 1) substr(b36, int(n / 36) % 36 + 1, 1) substr(b36, n % 36 + 1, 1)
  }
  function id_of(f,    id, cut, salt) {
    id = tolower(feature[f])
    gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, "-", id)
    gsub(/^-+|-+$/, "", id)
    if (id == feature[f] && length(id) + 1 + length(num[f]) <= room) return id
    cut = substr(id, 1, room - length(num[f]) - 5)
    gsub(/-+$/, "", cut)
    # Another feature on the same hashed id rehashes, so no two share one.
    salt = ""
    id = cut "_" hash(feature[f])
    while ((id in owner) && owner[id] != feature[f]) id = cut "_" hash(feature[f] "#" ++salt)
    owner[id] = feature[f]
    return id
  }
  /^\036/ {
    f = substr($0, 2)
    files[++n] = f
    split(f, part, "/")
    feature[f] = part[2]
    features[tolower(part[2])] = part[2]
    name[f] = part[4]
    num[f] = name[f]
    sub(/-.*/, "", num[f])
    issue[part[2] "/" (num[f] + 0)] = f
    comments = 0
    listing = 0
    next
  }
  { line = tolower($0) }
  line ~ /^#+[ \t]*comments[ \t]*$/ { comments = 1 }
  comments { next }
  !(f in title) && /^#[ \t]/ {
    title[f] = $0
    sub(/^#[ \t]+/, "", title[f]); sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", title[f])
  }
  !(f in labels) && line ~ /^[ \t*_]*status[ \t*_]*:/ {
    s = value(line)
    gsub(/[ \t,]+/, " ", s)
    labels[f] = " " s " "
  }
  listing && line ~ /^[ \t]*[-*+][ \t]/ {
    sub(/^[ \t]*[-*+][ \t]+/, "", line)
    blockers[f] = blockers[f] "," line
    next
  }
  listing && line !~ /^[ \t]*$/ { listing = 0 }
  !(f in blockers) && line ~ /^[ \t*_]*blocked by[ \t*_]*:/ {
    blockers[f] = value(line)
    listing = blockers[f] ~ /^[ \t]*$/
  }
  END {
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) ids[files[i]] = id_of(files[i])
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
      f = files[i]
      if (list == "backlog") {
        if (has(f, "blocked") || closed(f)) continue
        if (has(f, "ready-for-agent") && !has(f, "needs-info") \
            && !has(f, "ready-for-human")) continue
        if (!unblocked(f)) continue
        if (!(f in title)) { title[f] = name[f]; sub(/\.md$/, "", title[f]) }
        print f, title[f]
        continue
      }
      if (!has(f, "ready-for-agent") || has(f, "blocked") || has(f, "needs-info") \
          || has(f, "ready-for-human") || closed(f) || !unblocked(f)) continue
      type = "feat"; skill = "tdd"
      k = split(labels[f], words, " ")
      for (j = k; j >= 1; j--) {
        if (words[j] in types) type = types[words[j]]
        if (words[j] ~ /^skill:[a-z0-9._:-]+$/) skill = substr(words[j], 7)
      }
      slug = tolower(name[f])
      sub(/^[0-9]+-/, "", slug); sub(/\.md$/, "", slug)
      gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, " ", slug)
      k = split(slug, words, " ")
      slug = ""
      for (j = 1; j <= k && j <= 5; j++) slug = slug (j > 1 ? "-" : "") words[j]
      if (slug == "") slug = "issue"
      id = ids[f]
      if (length(id) + 1 + length(num[f]) > room) {
        print "skipped " f ": the herd name leaves no room for its id" > "/dev/stderr"
        continue
      }
      id = id "-" num[f]
      print id, type, skill, slug, f
    }
  }'

max = 3

[template.issue]
params = ["id", "type", "skill", "slug", "path"]
name = "{herd}-{id}"
branch = "{type}/{id}-{slug}"
# Done once origin/main has the issue's Status: line resolved, closed or done, and
# not done while the file is missing there. Braces are doubled, as loopherd
# fills {placeholders} in checks.
done = '''
git fetch -q origin main 2>/dev/null || git fetch -q origin main || exit
git cat-file -e origin/main:{path} 2>/dev/null || exit 1
text=$(git show origin/main:{path}) && printf '%s\n' "$text" | awk '
  {{ sub(/\r$/, "") }}
  tolower($0) ~ /^#+[ \t]*comments[ \t]*$/ {{ exit }}
  tolower($0) ~ /^[ \t*_]*status[ \t*_]*:/ {{
    s = tolower($0); sub(/^[^:]*:/, "", s); gsub(/[*`,]/, " ", s)
    closed = " " s " " ~ /[ \t](resolved|closed|done)[ \t]/
    exit
  }}
  END {{ exit !closed }}'
'''
merged = "GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr list --repo acme/widgets --head {branch} --state merged --json number --jq 'length > 0' | grep -qx true"
prompt = '''
You're {name}, working the local issue {path} on branch {branch} in
{worktree}. The issue is a markdown file in the repo; its `Status:` line near
the top holds its triage state, and comments go under a `## Comments` heading
at the bottom.

Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)` as in the commands below.

1. Read {path} in full, comments included.
2. Claim it: set its `Status:` line to `claimed`, append `claimed by {name}`
   under `## Comments` (adding the heading if it's missing), and commit.
3. Build it with the {skill} skill.
4. Before calling it done, run each check and fix what fails:
   - `cargo test`
   - `cargo fmt --check`
5. Set the issue's `Status:` line to `resolved`, append a one-line summary of
   the work under `## Comments`, and commit, so the issue closes when your
   branch merges.
6. Push the branch as acme:
   `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push -u origin HEAD`.
   Open a PR with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr create --repo acme/widgets --base main --head {branch} --assignee acme --title "<title>" --body "<summary>"`.
7. Finish with `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.

If main moves under you, merge origin/main into your branch; never
rebase or force-push.

If you hit a question only the human can answer, stop rather than guess: set
the issue's `Status:` line to `needs-info`, append the question and the
options you see under `## Comments`, commit and push the branch, then
`loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
'''

[lead]
prompt_file = "widgets-lead.md"
# From [lead_defaults] when init ran. Off means the lead asks the human.
merge = false
install = false
rebase = false
new_cards = false
design_escalation = false
blocked_dialogs = false
follow_ups_ready = false
merge_guard = "hook"
== widgets-lead.md
You're {name}, the lead of herd {herd}, in {worktree}, a detached checkout of
acme/widgets you never commit in. No human is in this pane.

Read `loopherd --skill` in full, its Lead section most closely. Tasks are issue files under `.scratch/` on origin's main. A worker's branch sets its issue's `Status:` line to `resolved`, so the issue closes when the branch merges.
Run every gh command as acme, prefixed with
`GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme)`. You run the shepherd's loop for {herd}'s workers: feed, watch, verify
each worker's PR with a reviewer subagent, send only blocking findings back
to the member, and the after-merge steps.

Your switches (off means the human does it; ask with a question report):
{switches}

Your review-round limit: {review_rounds}.

Grilling is always the human's.

Start now:
1. `loopherd status` and `loopherd reports --all`, to see where the herd is.
2. `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`, then `loopherd feed {herd}` if it reads right.
3. Arm `loopherd watch {herd} --timeout 3600` as a background task, and
   re-arm after every exit but `{herd} drained`: on that, report done and
   stop. On `<member> merged`, run `loopherd feed {herd}`,
   which retires it once its issue is closed. On `<name> claimable`, feed.
   Exit 2 is your heartbeat: check each worker's PR for a merge and run
   `loopherd feed {herd} --dry-run`.

When you need the human, run `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact
question>"` and end your turn. With merge off, a merge question carries the PR
link, any PR that must merge first, and the line
`! GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token --user acme) gh pr merge <n> --repo acme/widgets --merge --match-head-commit <full sha>`
for the head your reviewer verified. Single-quote that question ('...', not
"..."): double quotes run the $(...) and leak the token.
== AGENTS.md
# Agent instructions

## loopherd

A loopherd herd works this repo's ready issues, one worker per issue on its
own branch. A worker reads `docs/agents/loopherd.md` for how to claim, build,
check, hand in and report an issue, and `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` for
the tracker.
== docs/agents/issue-tracker.md
# Issue tracker: Local Markdown

Issues and specs for this repo live as markdown files under `.scratch/`.

## Conventions

- One feature per directory: `.scratch/<feature-slug>/`.
- The feature's spec is `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`.
- One file per implementation issue: `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, never in one combined tickets file.
- Triage state is a `Status:` line near the top of each issue file, using the strings in `triage-labels.md`.
- Comments and the rest of the conversation append to the bottom of the file under a `## Comments` heading.

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a new file under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/`, creating the directory if needed.

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read the file at the referenced path. Usually the user hands over the path or the issue number.

## Wayfinding operations

`/wayfinder` works through these. Its **map** is one file, and each ticket is a **child** file beside it.

- **Map**: `.scratch/<effort>/map.md`, holding the Notes, Decisions-so-far and Fog sections.
- **Child ticket**: `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, its body stating the question. A `Type:` line names the ticket type (`research`, `prototype`, `grilling` or `task`), and a `Status:` line reads `claimed` or `resolved`.
- **Blocking**: a `Blocked by: NN, NN` line near the top. The ticket unblocks once every file it names is `resolved`.
- **Frontier**: look through `.scratch/<effort>/issues/` for files that are open, unblocked and unclaimed, and take the lowest number.
- **Claim**: set `Status: claimed` and save the file before starting.
- **Resolve**: write the answer under an `## Answer` heading, set `Status: resolved`, then add a pointer (a one-line gist and a link) to Decisions-so-far in `map.md`.
== docs/agents/triage-labels.md
# Triage Labels

The skills speak in five canonical triage roles. This file maps each role to
the label string this repo's issue tracker uses.

| Label in mattpocock/skills | Label in our tracker | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `needs-triage` | `needs-triage` | Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue |
| `needs-info` | `needs-info` | Waiting on reporter for more information |
| `ready-for-agent` | `ready-for-agent` | Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent |
| `ready-for-human` | `ready-for-human` | Requires human implementation |
| `wontfix` | `wontfix` | Will not be actioned |

When a skill mentions a role, use the corresponding label string from this
table. Edit the "Label in our tracker" column to match the labels you use.
== docs/agents/loopherd.md
# Working an issue in a loopherd herd

Issues are markdown files under `.scratch/<feature>/issues/`. An issue's
triage state is the `Status:` line near its top, and comments go under a
`## Comments` heading at its bottom.

loopherd starts one worker per ready issue, each in its own worktree on its
own branch. The worker's prompt names the issue, the branch and the exact
commands; this doc says what each step is for. How the tracker works is in
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

## Claiming

Read the issue file in full first. Then set its `Status:` line to `claimed`,
append `claimed by <member>` under `## Comments`, with your member name, and
commit on your branch. Every gh command runs as acme.

## Branch names

`<type>/<id>-<slug>`: the id is the feature and the issue's number; the type
comes from the words of its `Status:` line through the herd file's type map
(by default `fix` for `bug`, `docs` for `documentation`, else `feat`); the
slug comes from the file name.
loopherd creates the branch and its worktree; work only there. If main
moves under you, merge `origin/main` into your branch; never rebase or
force-push.

## Checks

Before calling the work done, run each check and fix what fails:

- `cargo test`
- `cargo fmt --check`

## Handing in

Before pushing, set the issue's `Status:` line to `resolved` and append a
one-line summary under `## Comments`, so merging the branch closes the issue;
loopherd counts the issue done once main has it resolved. Push the branch and open a PR with `--base main`.

## Stopping on a question

When only the human can answer, stop rather than guess: set the issue's
`Status:` line to `needs-info`, append the question and the options you see
under `## Comments`, commit and push, then report it.

## Reporting

Tell the shepherd how the work ended:

- Done: `loopherd report --kind done "<PR link and one-line summary>"`.
- Stopped on a question: `loopherd report --kind question "<the exact question>"`.
